text:
maya: Ran a long-context stress run on dedicated-qa and seeing KV cache mem growth that doesn't drop between requests. Repro: 100k tokens churn across 3 concurrent sessions, memory steadily climbs.

jia: Can you paste a short snippet from the runtime logs where you see the stale entries? :eyes:

maya: Sure. Snip:
```
INFO kv_page_write page=3456 offset=128 len=64 req_id=req-42 tag=0xabc123 owner_session=U234
INFO kv_page_read  page=3456 offset=128 len=64 req_id=req-43 tag=0xabc123 owner_session=U237 -> stale_owner_mismatch
WARN kv_evict      page=3456 tombstone=true discovered_cross_owner=true
```
This is from a run where req-42 finished 20s before req-43 started, but the tag and payload are identical and owner_session differs.

sam: That looks like cross-request contamination rather than just fragmentation. Did you turn on the new batching heuristic in that run (the merge-small-pages change)?

maya: Yes, it was on. We flipped merge_small_pages=true to reduce small-page overhead. The change was in runtime/serve/batcher.cc @ c3a9b7f.

oliver: c3a9b7f was the commit that introduced the pooled-slab reuse for KV appends. I remember a FIXME about zeroing the tail when reusing. Could be reusing a page buffer without updating the session tag.

dmitri: Repro steps I'd try:
- run long_context_repro.py (tests/perf/long_context_repro.py) with --sessions 3 --tokens 100000
- enable KV_WARN_ON_OWNER_MISMATCH env var to log mismatches with stack traces
- run with ASAN build if possible to catch out-of-bounds

maya: I ran the repro with KV_WARN_ON_OWNER_MISMATCH set and got a stack trace pointing to kv_page_append then kv_page_commit. The commit path looks normal, but the append path can be called concurrently from the batching code.

jia: Could be a race between appending and rotating the slot: one thread appends to a reused slab, another rotates and writes tombstone metadata but doesn't flush the per-request tag update in time. If the metadata write isn't atomic with the payload, readers can see the old tag.

perf-bot: CI perf/regression: runtime/kv_mem_per_1M_tokens +2.4% (regression window 2026-02-10..2026-02-14) link: https://perf.redwood.example/dashboard/kv_mem

sam: The perf delta aligns with when merge_small_pages landed in staging. We should bisect between previous working commit and c3a9b7f. Also check kernel selection changes — did any kernel rewrite affect KV memcpy paths (vectorized vs scalar)? Those can reorder stores on some ARM GPUs.

oliver: I instrumented a build locally adding an assert in kv_page_commit:
```
assert(page->owner_session == current_req->session_id, "owner mismatch at commit: %s -> %s");
```
It fired after ~200k tokens in the repro. The interesting bit: owner_session looked updated, but snapshot_owner (a separate header) still had old value until an explicit flush of 16 bytes was done.

dmitri: That smells like a false sharing / cacheline write-order problem. We have two adjacent fields in the header: payload_tag (8 bytes) and owner_session (8 bytes). If we write owner_session then payload in two non-atomic stores, another core can read interleaved values.

maya: Work plan:
1) Turn on header-level tombstone fencing so commit writes header with a single 16-byte atomic (or memcpy followed by memory_barrier).
2) Add extra zeroing when reusing slab buffers (oliver's FIXME).
3) Run bisect to confirm c3a9b7f is the culprit; if not, test kernel memcpy variants.
4) Add a short, deterministic unit test that does: append+rotate+read across threads to detect this class of bug.

jia: I can own the fence+unit test. Sam/Dmitri can help with bisect and performance guardrails to make sure fencing doesn't regress throughput too much.

sam: For bisect: start at 2061200000 (last known good)..2063000000 (first bad in staging runs). I'll run binary search on staging infra and report back.

maya: Repro commands for the team (from dedicated-qa node):
```
# reproduce
python3 tests/perf/long_context_repro.py --ws-url http://qa-runtime:8080 --sessions 3 --tokens 100000 --prompt-file tests/data/long_prompts.txt
# enable verbose kv warnings
KV_WARN_ON_OWNER_MISMATCH=1 RUNTIME_LOG=kv=debug ./bazel-bin/runtime/serve
```

oliver: Also add an experiment with MERGE_SMALL_PAGES=false to confirm perf and correctness baseline.

dmitri: If fencing fixes correctness but the perf hit is >1% per-1M tokens, we can try a hybrid: fence only when slab_reuse_count > 0 or in dedicated builds. But correctness first.

maya: I'll open an issue and a draft PR with the fence and the slab-zero fix. Linking the logs and stack traces in the issue. Thanks all — will post updates. :thumbsup:
